Tension in Bera as leaders of BNP and activities-banned Awami League confront each other
item.description:
The situation in Bera municipal area of Pabna remains tense today, Sunday. In the morning, leaders and activists of the ruling BNP and the Awami League, whose activities are banned, continued to face each other in several parts of the municipality.

According to eyewitnesses, leaders and activists of the Awami League and Jubo League, have gathered in the neighbourhoods of Sambhupur and Payna. Meanwhile, BNP leaders and activists have assembled in the Hatigara area.

Sambhupur, Payna and Hatigara are neighbouring areas. The presence of the two groups facing each other has created tension in the locality. Police have taken up positions between the two sides to prevent clashes and violence.

In view of the situation, most shops at Dakbangla Bazar remain closed. However, some shops have opened at Bera Market. Fear among residents has also reduced the number of people visiting the markets.

OC withdrawn at night

Following repeated clashes over the past three days between leaders and activists of the ruling BNP and Awami League, Noyan Kumar Sarkar, officer-in-charge of Bera Model Police Station, was withdrawn on Saturday night. He has been attached to the Rajshahi Reserve Range (RRF).

Inspector Golam Mostofa of Pabna Sadar Circle has taken charge as the new OC of Bera Police Station. Pabna Superintendent of Police Abu Ashraf confirmed the development.

At around 11:30 am today, Sunday, the new OC, Golam Mostofa, told Prothom Alo, “I have visited various parts of the municipality since this morning. Although people have gathered in some areas, the overall situation remains normal. I hope the situation will not deteriorate any further.”

Clashes and tension since Thursday

Police and local sources said tension and clashes between the two groups began in different neighbourhoods of Bera municipality on Thursday, 19 November. On that day, leaders and activists of the Awami League, Jubo League and their affiliated organisations from Sambhupur and Payna gathered in front of Bera Police Station after bringing out a procession.

Clashes broke out when BNP and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal leaders and activists chased them. The two groups also clashed in the Brishalikha neighbourhood on the same day.

Several houses came under attack, with incidents of vandalism and arson. One of the properties was the abandoned house of former Deputy Speaker and Awami League leader Shamsul Haque Tuku.

On Friday, BNP leaders and activists from the neighbouring Hatigara area exchanged chases with leaders and activists of the Awami League in Sambhupur and Payna. Following these incidents, tension spread across the municipality again from Saturday morning.

On Saturday morning, local Member of Parliament Selim Reza Habib, Deputy Commissioner Aminul Islam, Superintendent of Police Abu Ashraf, other administrative officials and local BNP leaders held a meeting to discuss measures to bring the situation under control.

During the meeting, local BNP leaders and activists expressed their anger, alleging that the police had failed to control the clashes.

Eyewitnesses said that, after the meeting, OC Noyan Kumar Sarkar visited Hatigara to assess the situation. Some local residents also expressed their anger over the police's role. At that point, a journalist who was recording the incident on video was harassed, and his camera was vandalised.

Soon afterwards, fresh clashes broke out between the two groups in front of Shamsul Hoque Tuku's house in Brishalikha. The violence subsequently spread to several neighbouring areas. The situation came under control towards the evening.

At least 25 people reportedly sustained injuries in Saturday's clashes. Among them was a teenager from Hatigara who suffered serious injuries.

item.title: Factories to be handed over to the private sector
item.description:
The government will bring all factories under the Ministry of Industries, except fertiliser factories, under private-sector investment. In other words, the government wants the factories to be operated by the private sector. The process may begin early next year after the necessary rules and regulations are approved.

Industries Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said this in response to a question at a press conference held at the Ministry of Industries yesterday, Saturday. He said, “We will invite private sector investment in all factories except fertiliser factories. This will be done under the PPP model.”

The minister said there are several methods under public-private partnership (PPP). One involves long-term leasing, another revenue sharing, and another profit sharing. The factories will be handed over under one of these three methods.

Besides fertiliser factories, the industries ministry oversees factories producing sugar and food products, cement, steel, chemicals and other goods. Most of these factories incur losses year after year. According to the revised figures for the 2023–24 fiscal year, their annual losses amounted to more than Tk 20 billion.

Before the 13th parliamentary election, the BNP’s election manifesto promised to reopen closed factories. Subsequently, the process of handing over jute and textile mills to the private sector began. Several factories have already been handed over to the private sector. The Ministry of Industries is also pursuing the same process.

The government is not injecting more taxpayers’ money to reopen these factories; rather, it is trying to restart them through the private sector.

After the press conference, Prothom Alo contacted Industries Minister and Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir again yesterday evening. Asked about handing over all factories under the Ministry of Industries, except fertiliser factories, to the private sector, he said, “Once the process begins, it takes at least six months to complete. We will begin the tendering process transparently from January next year. We hope to receive a good response.”

Government-owned factories

After the country’s independence, the government nationalised factories in various sectors, bringing them under state ownership. On 26 March 1972, the first anniversary of independence, then Prime Minister Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman announced the nationalisation of large industries.

Under this order, all factories in the jute, textile and sugar industries, as well as other industrial enterprises with assets worth more than Tk 1.5 million, came under government ownership.

However, due to a lack of management, excessive unnecessary recruitment based on political considerations, corruption and the failure to make new investments, the factories fell into decline. Meanwhile, the private sector developed.

Government-owned factories are, overall, loss-making. Some of them make a small profit. In the 2023–24 fiscal year, factories in the industrial sector incurred losses of Tk 22.47 billion. Eleven years earlier, in 2013–14, the amount of losses was Tk 8.84 billion. During this period, government-owned industrial factories did not make an overall profit in any year.

Mustafizur Rahman, distinguished fellow at the non-government research organisation Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), views the initiative to hand over state-owned industrial factories to the private sector positively.

He told Prothom Alo, “The time has come to rethink our state-owned enterprises. These institutions have been running at a loss year after year. They are being kept alive with taxpayers’ money. There is no way to deny the need for reforms in this sector.”

Mustafizur Rahman said, however, that how each institution is handed over and what safeguards are put in place are extremely important. Regardless of how they are handed over, it must be ensured that they continue to operate as industrial factories. The initiative must not in any way create opportunities for buying and selling land, and it must be ensured that factory land is not used for real estate businesses.

Factories under the industries ministry

The Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation (BSFIC), under the Ministry of Industries, began operations in 1976. The corporation currently controls 15 sugar mills, one engineering factory and two commercial establishments.

Six of the corporation’s 15 sugar mills remain closed throughout the year. Several others operate during the sugarcane-crushing season. The closed mills are Kushtia Sugar Mills, Panchagarh Sugar Mills, Pabna Sugar Mills, Rangpur Sugar Mills, Shyampur Sugar Mills and Setabganj Sugar Mills. In the 2022–23 fiscal year, BSFIC incurred losses of Tk 5.33 billion.

The Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC) began operations in 1972. At the time, it had 88 factories. Six new factories were subsequently established, and three factories were transferred to BCIC from other organisations. However, at different times, BCIC factories have been closed, handed over to the private sector or returned to their previous owners. Seven factories were also handed over to the Muktijoddha Kalyan Trust.

According to BCIC data, 11 factories are currently operational. Of these, seven are fertiliser factories. There is one factory each for paper, cement, glass sheets, and sanitary ware and insulators. BCIC incurred losses of Tk 8.75 billion in the 2022–23 fiscal year.

Initially, 62 industrial enterprises were under the control of the Bangladesh Steel and Engineering Corporation (BSEC). In 1984, it established Bangladesh Blade Factory Limited. Currently, nine industrial enterprises are operational under the corporation’s management.

Of these, 49 per cent of the shares in Atlas Bangladesh Limited, National Tubes Limited and Eastern Cables Limited have been floated on the capital market.

The government owns 100 per cent of the shares in Eastern Tubes, Gazi Wires Limited, General Electric Manufacturing Company, Pragati Industries, Bangladesh Blade Factory and Dhaka Steel Works.

In 2013, BSEC acquired a 30 per cent stake in Bangladesh Honda Private Limited through a joint venture with Japan’s Honda. BSEC owns slightly more than 25 per cent of the shares in The General Electric Company of Bangladesh in Chattogram.

Successive governments have provided loans worth millions of taka to keep various factories operational. According to the Bangladesh Economic Survey 2025, the government’s outstanding loans and interest owed by the Sugar and Food Industries Corporation amount to Tk 86.25 billion, by BCIC to Tk 82.36 billion and by BSEC to Tk 1.95 billion.

Hopes for foreign investment

Foreign and domestic investors are interested in investing in factories under the Ministry of Industries. For example, Japan’s Marubeni Corporation has expressed interest in investing in the modernisation of the country’s operational sugar mills and establishing new production facilities at closed sugar mills.

Through Marubeni Protech Corporation, it wants to install modern machinery at three sugar mills in the western region of the country. To this end, a Marubeni delegation met the chairman of BSFIC last week.

There are two differing views among analysts regarding government-owned factories. Some support keeping the factories under government ownership. They believe that factories are necessary if the government is to maintain control over the product market. The other side sees no reason to keep factories under government ownership when they have been incurring losses year after year.

Zahid Hussain, former lead economist at the World Bank’s Dhaka office, believes that how the factories are handed over to the private sector is important. If the factories are transferred to genuine businesspeople through a competitive process, and if this creates opportunities for production and employment, it will be good for the country. In his view, factories must not be handed over to oligarchs in the name of privatisation.

Referring to the closure of Adamjee Jute Mills, Zahid Hossain told Prothom Alo that around 25,000 people had lost their jobs there. As a result of establishing an export processing zone, employment was created for around 100,000 people.

item.title: Bangladesh needs to increase investment in education and health sectors
item.description:
Catherine Russell is the eighth Executive Director of the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF). She assumed office on 1 February 2022. Before that, from 2020 to 2022, she served as Assistant to US President Joe Biden and Director of the White House Office of Presidential Personnel. From 2013 to 2017, she served as the United States Ambassador-at-Large for Global Women's Issues.

Catherine Russell visited Bangladesh from 17 to 19 October, taking part in various activities related to children's rights. During her visit, Prothom Alo sent UNICEF a set of written questions on issues concerning children's rights, including the measles outbreak, vaccine shortages, child marriage, health, and education. The interview was conducted by Prothom Alo's Naznin Akhtar.

We observed Child Rights Week and International Day of the Girl Child in October. How would you assess the overall situation of children's rights in Bangladesh? In which areas has the country made progress, and which children are still being left behind?

Catherine Russell: Bangladesh has made considerable progress in improving the lives of children. However, despite this progress, some major challenges remain. Bangladesh is among the countries in Asia with the highest rates of child marriage. What is particularly concerning is that not all children in Bangladesh are benefiting equally from the country's progress. Girls at risk of child marriage and violence, children with disabilities, children from poor families, street children, and those living in remote and climate-vulnerable areas need additional support and attention. The same applies to Rohingya refugee children.

The remarkable resilience of children and young people in Bangladesh gives me hope. The adolescent girls I met in Dhaka and Cox's Bazar told me that they would not give up dreaming about their future. Like all other children, they need opportunities to access education, healthcare, and protection.

Bangladesh has made progress in reducing child mortality and increasing children's school enrolment. However, millions of children still live or work on the streets. What should be the country's top priority for children over the next five years?

Catherine Russell: Over the past five decades, Bangladesh has made significant progress in reducing child mortality and improving children's access to education. But this cannot be considered complete success when millions of children are still being left out of these gains. During my visit to Korail, I saw how growing up without parental care and protection can affect a child's life. A significant number of children in Bangladesh live on the streets without parental protection. Many of them are forced into child labour.

According to the 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS), conducted with support from UNICEF, the rate of child labour, which stood at 6.8 per cent in 2019, rose to 9.2 per cent in 2025. In my view, Bangladesh's foremost priority over the next five years should be to ensure that the benefits of progress reach even the most disadvantaged children. Children must be protected from violence, exploitation, and child marriage. They must be kept in school, and their access to essential healthcare must be ensured.

I welcome the government's plan to invest 5 per cent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP) each in the education and health sectors. However, these resources must reach the children and communities that need them most. During my visit, I saw that Bangladesh has enormous potential. Over the next five years, the country's success will be measured by how far economic growth translates into lasting improvements in the lives of its most vulnerable children.

According to the 2025 MICS report, 56 per cent of girls in Bangladesh are married before reaching the age of 18. Despite the existence of laws prohibiting child marriage, the practice continues. Why has the law failed to bring about sufficient change in the real-life context?

Catherine Russell: During my visit to Korail, I met a 14-year-old girl whose child marriage had been prevented through the intervention of a child protection centre run by UNICEF in support of the Bangladesh government. She told me that she had fought to fulfil her dreams. She wants to become a pilot.

Bangladesh has the highest rate of child marriage in South Asia. It is also among the 10 countries with the highest rates of child marriage in the world. This situation underscores the need for legal reform. UNICEF is working to amend the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017 by removing the provision that allows marriage before the age of 18 under certain circumstances (Section 19, Special Provision).

If Bangladesh is to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal of ending child marriage by 2030, it must act swiftly to bring about meaningful and effective change.

Around 17 million children are living in multidimensional poverty. Many more children belong to families that could fall into poverty following even a minor setback. These challenges remind us that success cannot be measured solely by the number of children we have reached

UNICEF has been working to end child marriage in Bangladesh for several decades. What lessons has the organisation learned about which initiatives have not worked, and what changes are now needed?

Catherine Russell: One lesson is clear: laws alone cannot transform girls' lives unless they are effectively enforced and accompanied by practical action at the grassroots level. It is also essential to increase the number and strengthen the capacity of social service workers so that those most at risk receive the support they need.

We must also address issues such as access to quality education and skills development, healthcare, and protection from gender-based violence. These barriers need to be overcome through coordinated initiatives and policy reforms.

UNICEF has been working in Bangladesh for several decades. In your opinion, in which areas has the organisation succeeded, and where do gaps remain?

Catherine Russell: UNICEF can take pride in the work we have accomplished over the past five decades in partnership with the Government of Bangladesh and other partners. Child mortality has declined. Poverty and deprivation have decreased. Millions of children now have access to better healthcare and nutrition services. Immunisation programmes have expanded significantly. Access to safe water and sanitation has improved considerably. The number of children attending school has also increased. UNICEF has contributed to these achievements by strengthening national systems and helping deliver essential services.

However, the benefits of this progress have yet to reach every child. Around 17 million children are living in multidimensional poverty. Many more children belong to families that could fall into poverty following even a minor setback. These challenges remind us that success cannot be measured solely by the number of children we have reached. We must also consider whether we are bringing about lasting improvements in their lives. More work is needed to address the root causes of deprivation, including poverty, harmful social practices, unequal access to services, and inadequate investment in children.

Programmes, policies, and budgets must be guided by evidence of what works. Through consultations with children and young people, the Child Rights Manifesto was developed with UNICEF's support. Twelve political parties have endorsed it. This has helped bring children's priorities into the national discourse and build a collective commitment to advancing them.

What is your principal recommendation to the Government of Bangladesh for strengthening children's rights and ensuring that no child is left behind?

Catherine Russell: As I also said during my discussion with State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, my central message to the new government is that children must be placed at the heart of Bangladesh's national development plans, and political commitments must be translated into concrete action.

First, adolescent girls must be protected, and opportunities must be created for them to realise their full potential. Strong measures are needed to ensure that girls can continue their education, remain protected from all forms of violence and child marriage, and have access to essential healthcare. It is crucial to remove the special provision from the Child Marriage Restraint Act 2017.

Second, investment in education and health must be increased. Allocated funds must be released on time and used effectively and equitably so that children in disadvantaged areas can also benefit.

Third, educational and skills-development opportunities must be expanded for both Rohingya and host-community children. By providing shelter to more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees, Bangladesh has demonstrated extraordinary generosity. However, more than 150,000 Rohingya children are still out of school. We encourage the government to expand access to safe learning spaces and skills-development opportunities for children from both the Rohingya and host communities.

Thank you for your time.

Catherine Russell: Thank you, too.

item.title: Harpic to take hygiene lessons to 500,000 children, launches animated series on World Toilet Day
item.description:
Harpic Bangladesh plans to bring hygiene education to 500,000 children through its hygiene curriculum next year and will continue working for under-privileged children and families, reports a press release.

The brand made the announcement at Harpic Toilet Talk 2026, held in the capital ahead of World Toilet Day.

The event, held at Le Méridien Dhaka under the global theme of this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Safe Toilets. Equal Futures,” also marked the launch of a 10-episode animated series for children featuring Dipu and Tushi, the familiar characters from Harpic’s hygiene comic introduced last year. Fulfilling its commitment to extend hygiene education to children, Harpic brought this initiative to life through the animated series.

It was organised by Harpic Bangladesh in association with its partners Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC), SAJIDA Foundation, Gana Unnayan Kendra (GUK) and Mojar School.

Md Golam Muktadir, project director of the Department of Public Health Engineering (DPHE), while delivering the keynote address, he highlighted that despite Bangladesh’s significant progress in sanitation, achieving SDG targets remains a major challenge with 109 million people still lacking access to safely managed sanitation.

The programme opened with welcome remarks from Tabasser Ahmed, senior brand manager of Reckitt Bangladesh.

A panel discussion was followed, moderated by Md Rakib Uddin, manager of external affairs at Reckitt Bangladesh.

The panelists were Sabrin Maruf Tinni, head of marketing, Reckitt Bangladesh; Air Commodore Md Mahabubur Rahman Talukder, chief waste management officer (CWMO), DSCC; Captain Ikhtiar Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, chief waste management officer (CWMO), DNCC; Md Fazlul Hoque, deputy CEO, SAJIDA Foundation; and Arian Arif, founder and executive director, Mojar School.

The discussion centered on strengthening sanitation infrastructure in the capital, improving waste management and making sanitation facilities inclusive.

Speakers agreed that city authorities, development organisations and the private sector need to work together to close the gap between toilet access and safe sanitation.

Captain Ikhtiar Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, chief waste management officer (CWMO), DNCC emphasised on the need to expand sanitation facilities across the city, highlighting the importance of increasing access to safe, hygienic and inclusive toilets to ensure better sanitation for all.

“We want to create awareness, educate people and encourage lasting change in behaviour. At Harpic, our responsibility goes beyond promoting products,” said Sabrin Maruf Tinni.

She also mentioned that the brand wants to make hygiene education accessible and engaging for children through storytelling and digital content creators.

“Ultimately, it is about helping people understand why hygiene matters and making safe practices part of everyday life,” she added.

The new animated series, Dipu-Tushir Hygiene Abhijan, uses short, entertaining stories to help children build good personal hygiene and toilet habits. The series will be available on Harpic Bangladesh’s social platforms.

More than 30 digital content creators attended the event to take hygiene lessons nationwide, which also featured interactive engagement zones on sanitation and hygiene.

Harpic, Reckitt’s flagship toilet care brand, has been in Bangladesh since 1978 and is the country’s leading toilet cleaner.

World Toilet Day is a United Nations observance held every year on 19 November to raise awareness of the global sanitation crisis and the need for safe sanitation for all.

item.title: DNCC cleaners to get 784 flats, handover within three and a half months
item.description:
Cleaners work from midnight until dawn to keep the city clean. It is through their labour that city dwellers see a clean city every morning. Yet many of these cleaners live in unhealthy and dilapidated environments. Now, four 15-storey buildings have been built for their housing, offering 784 flats for their families.

The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) has built the housing complex at Gabtoli City Palli in the capital. Visiting the site last Tuesday, four residential buildings were found standing side by side. Buildings W-2, W-3 and W-4 have 16 flats on each floor, totalling 672 flats. Building W-5, meanwhile, has eight flats on each floor, totalling 112. Together, the four buildings have 784 flats.

Each flat measures 565 square feet and has two bedrooms, a separate room for children, a kitchen, a toilet and a bathroom. There are also separate spaces for a drawing room and dining area. The main bedroom comes with a balcony.

A visit to the buildings found that the finishing work had been completed, including floor tiles, wall paint, electrical lights and fans. Kitchen sinks have also been installed.

The buildings with 16 flats on each floor have six lifts, while the building with eight flats per floor has two. Each building has two regular staircases and two additional staircases for emergency exits.

However, the flats have not yet been handed over as gas connections and the allocation process remain incomplete. DNCC aims to hand them over within three and a half months.

Dhaka North City has around 2400 cleaners, of whom about 800, including their families live in Gabtoli. They were previously living in Gulshan before being relocated to Gabtoli in 2005.

Regarding flat allocation, DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan told Prothom Alo that officials have been given the responsibility to verify who is eligible to receive the flats, taking into consideration the cleaners' length of service and other criteria. DNCC's chief estate officer and officials from its waste management department are preparing the list.

He said a specific set of criteria will be fixed to ensure no one feels deprived of an allocation. Efforts will be made to allocate flats transparently, keeping in view those who have been in service for a long time and those deserving of priority.

The administrator said it may take at least another three to three and a half months to complete the remaining work, including gas connections. They hope to finalize the allocation list within this timeframe. He also mentioned plans to have the Prime Minister inaugurate the project.

Raju Gazi, executive president of the Scavengers and Workers Union, an organisation of cleaners working for Dhaka North City, told Prothom Alo that the authorities have yet to hold any formal discussion with them about flat allocation.

“There has been no formal discussion between the authorities and us regarding the allocation yet. However, we have heard that those with longer service tenures will be prioritized. But we have mentioned that the affected cleaners who were displaced from Gulshan and relocated to Gabtoli should be given flats in that building,” he said.

Gas connections underway

Although the kitchens have provisions for gas connections, construction of the central gas plant has not yet been completed. DNCC is carrying out the work through a separate tender. Gas will be supplied to each flat through individual connections from the central plant, meaning residents will not have to buy or store gas cylinders separately.

The ground floors of the buildings have been designated for social gatherings. Residents will be able to hold family and social events there. Initially, however, the open ground-floor areas had no grills or gates for security. Following instructions from DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan after he took office, work has begun to enclose the ground floors with brick walls and iron grills. Collapsible gates will also be installed.

A four-storey school building has been constructed within the project area for the children of cleaners. DNCC has also signed a memorandum of understanding with a non-governmental development organisation to run the school.

The entire residential complex has also been equipped with firefighting facilities, a dedicated substation for electricity supply and a solar power plant for backup.

The project, titled ‘Construction of Multistoried Cleaners Residential Complex at Gabtoli City Polli under Dhaka North City Corporation’, cost Tk 2.8473 billion.

The project was initially launched in 2017 with a budget of Tk 1.17 billion, with completion scheduled for June 2019. Subsequently, the project was revised and its costs increased three times — to Tk 2.21 billion in the first revision, Tk 2.49 billion in the second and Tk 2.84 billion in the third.

The deadline for completion in the third phase was until December of last year. However, without increasing the cost further, the project tenure was extended once until June of this year.

Rafiqul Islam, supervisory engineer (electrical) at DNCC, is serving as the project's sixth director. He told Prothom Alo that complications regarding fund allocations arose during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, bringing work nearly to a halt at one point.

Although the project was funded by the government, the city corporation had to pay the contractor from its own funds to keep the work going at the time, he said.

Rafiqul Islam said the main work of the project has now been completed. However, following the administrator's advice, some additional work is still being carried out, including the construction of a central gas plant to resolve the gas supply issue.

The flats would be handed over to the cleaners as soon as the remaining work was completed, he said.

item.title: Awami League attacks NCP members after Nahid’s reception in London: What happened that night
item.description:
It was 9:59 pm. Karin, a resident of Cedar Park Gardens in Chadwell Heath, east London, called the police emergency number. She still did not understand what had triggered the clash on the road outside her home. While she was speaking to the police, the violence escalated.

A group of people were taking glass bottles out of recycling bins and breaking branches off trees. They were even picking up stones and decorative items from the garden outside her house and throwing them at people on the opposite side of the road.

On Monday night, 16 November, a residential street in east London became a scene of tension over political divisions in Bangladesh.

Following a civic reception for Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party (NCP) and Chief Whip of the Opposition in the Jatiya Sangsad, leaders, activists and supporters from Awami League, whose activities are banned in Bangladesh, attacked NCP leaders and activists. The incident led to clashes between the two groups.

The NCP reported that 16 of its members had been injured, while the Awami League reported at least three injuries among its members.

However, figures from the London police and the London Ambulance Service show that fewer people received hospital treatment or medical assistance at the scene.

To find out how the incident was started, Prothom Alo spoke to at least 16 people, including eyewitnesses, local residents, journalists, activists and leaders from both political parties, as well as others familiar with the incident.

The newspaper also visited the scene and examined at least 20 videos of the incident. By comparing eyewitness accounts, video footage and information provided by the police, Prothom Alo sought to reconstruct how the incident began, how the clashes unfolded and how the violence continued.

Awami league-NCP supporters clash after Nahid Islam’s reception in London, 5 injured

A British resident calls the police

Karin, a resident of Cedar Park Gardens, told Prothom Alo that she heard some commotion on the street at around 8:00 pm on the night of the incident. However, the situation did not seem unusual at the time.

She thought a few men were arguing among themselves. She did not give much attention to the matter and even advised other residents against going outside out of curiosity to see what was happening.

Karin said, “I went to bed just before 10:00 pm. Suddenly, I heard much louder shouting, swearing and sounds of people hitting one another. I got out of bed and looked outside through the window. I saw many angry men, several security personnel and a few cars trying to leave the venue. At first, I thought there had been some misunderstanding among a few people attending the event.”

According to Karin, one security guard was speaking to the people present in an extremely rude and domineering manner.

When the guard walked past her window, she asked him what was happening. She felt that he was struggling to control the situation. He asked her to wait for a while before returning to the crowd. Karin then decided to call the police.

The Cedar Park Gardens resident said, “I called the police at 9:59 pm. By then, the situation had deteriorated. However, the violence reached its peak while I was still speaking to the police on the phone.”

She added, “Some people were taking glass bottles out of recycling bins, breaking branches off trees and picking up stones and decorative items from the garden outside my house. They were throwing these at people from the opposing group on the other side of the road.”

According to Karin, the police arrived at the scene within about 15 minutes of her call. Most of the crowd dispersed shortly after the police arrived. The time Karin called the police is consistent with the time mentioned in the Police statement.

Maria was too frightened to leave her home

Maria, another resident of the same street, was at home on the night of the incident. She told Prothom Alo that she could hear crowds gathering outside, people shouting, arguing loudly and fighting, all from inside her house. However, she was too frightened to go outside. Other members of her family went out and witnessed the incident.

Citing her family members, Maria said that people from both groups were throwing bottles at each other, breaking branches off roadside trees and trying to attack one another with them.

They were also picking up bricks from the front gardens of local residents' homes and throwing them at each other. Maria's family members were not at home when the correspondent visited the area, so it was not possible to obtain their accounts directly.

Another resident of Cedar Park Gardens witnessed the incident from his home that night. Speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, he said he had seen two groups of young men throwing glass bottles at each other.

They were collecting the bottles from garbage bins placed outside houses on both sides of the road. They were also breaking branches off roadside trees and chasing one another with them. He said he had seen them throwing not only bottles but also the garbage bins placed outside the houses at each other.

However, the resident could not identify anyone involved in the clashes. He also had no idea which political parties the people from either group were affiliated with.

The sudden outbreak of violence prompted many residents of the street to come out of their homes. Some watched from outside their houses, while others looked on through their windows.

Conversations with local residents revealed that they could not understand what had triggered the fighting or who was attacking whom. The violence in their residential neighbourhood left them frightened.

Why Awami League activists protesting only against NCP leaders in UK?

Calls to foil the visit had been made in advance

Ever since news emerged of Nahid Islam's visit to the United Kingdom, a section of Awami League leaders, activists and supporters based there had been announcing their intention to prevent him from carrying out his programmes.

Several Awami League activists used Facebook to announce protests against Nahid Islam at various events and declare their plans to foil his programmes.

Many people also received WhatsApp messages containing the addresses and timings of the planned demonstrations, urging them to attend. This correspondent also received one such message.

Earlier, Awami League-affiliated leaders and activists had staged another protest surrounding an event attended by Nahid Islam in Cambridge. They attempted to harass him, but NCP leaders and activists present at the venue thwarted their efforts.

As part of this continuing campaign, Awami League leaders, activists and supporters staged a protest on Monday surrounding Nahid Islam's civic reception in east London. They presented the demonstration as an exercise of their democratic right to protest.

Before the event began, guests were arriving at the Mayfair venue. A video shows one protester throwing a bottle of water at Barrister Saifuddin Khaled, a councillor of Tower Hamlets Council and former Speaker of the council, from among the demonstrators.

Police officers were present both at the front and rear of the hall before the event began. The police appeared to be actively working to control the demonstrators' shouting and the increasingly tense situation.

NCP’s strategy to move Nahid to safety

In anticipation of possible protests and obstruction by Awami League leaders and activists, the organisers arranged extensive security measures for the civic reception.

Alongside the police, the NCP hired more than 30 private security personnel. To avoid any potential disruption, Nahid Islam arrived at the Mayfair venue at least three hours before the event began.

A visit to the site revealed that the main entrance to the Mayfair venue faces High Road. Cedar Park Gardens, a residential street, runs behind the hall. Around halfway through this street are the hall’s rear entrance and the entry and exit routes to its car park.

The investigation found that, on the night of the incident, Awami League leaders and activists were positioned on the western side of the street, while NCP leaders and activists were on the eastern side.

According to information gathered during the investigation, the NCP had devised a strategy to ensure Nahid Islam could leave the venue safely. The plan was for party leaders and activists to leave through the hall’s main entrance and chant slogans.

This would lead Awami League leaders and activists to believe that Nahid Islam was also leaving through the front entrance. Meanwhile, Nahid Islam would leave the venue through the rear exit.

At 9:55 pm, Nahid Islam left the event through the rear exit with the assistance of security personnel. His car drove out through the car park access road connected to Cedar Park Gardens.

Meanwhile, NCP leaders and activists, led by central leader Barrister Nurul Huda Juned, came out through the main entrance and began chanting slogans. In this way, Nahid Islam left the venue safely without facing any untoward incident.

Glass bottles thrown and tree branches used in attacks

Prothom Alo spoke to two eyewitnesses who had no affiliation with either the Awami League or the NCP. They provided detailed accounts of the incident that day.

According to them, several Awami League leaders and activists were inside cars on Cedar Park Gardens during the incident. After hearing NCP leaders and activists chanting slogans near the front of the hall, they got out of their vehicles.

Meanwhile, NCP leaders and activists, led by Barrister Nurul Huda Juned, moved from the front of the hall towards the rear street. This correspondent personally saw Nurul Huda Juned leave the hall while chanting slogans.

According to the two eyewitnesses, Awami League members began hurling abuse at NCP leaders and activists. At one point, NCP members gathered and chased the Awami League members, forcing them towards the western end of the street.

There, they collected empty glass bottles from waste bins placed outside houses and began throwing them at NCP leaders and activists. The eyewitnesses said a glass bottle struck an NCP activist on the head.

Awami League leaders and activists then broke branches off roadside trees and chased their NCP counterparts with them.

Local resident Karin and another resident also described how people threw bottles, broke tree branches and used various objects taken from outside residents’ homes to attack the opposing group. However, it has not been possible to establish who first resorted to physical violence.

The eyewitnesses said that, after the Awami League members chased them, NCP leaders and activists moved towards High Road, the street in front of the hall. They then tried to re-enter the venue.

However, in response to the situation, the hall authorities closed the shutters at the main entrance to protect their premises. As a result, NCP leaders and activists could not immediately take shelter inside.

Shakir Hossain, president of the Bangladesh Press Club UK and editor of AB News, told Prothom Alo, “After chasing NCP leaders and activists from Cedar Park Gardens, Awami League members beat them with sticks and tree branches.” Several videos circulating on social media show people being assaulted at the entrance to the hall.

Conflicting accounts from the two sides

The Awami League and the NCP have offered different accounts of how the clashes began.

Barrister Nurul Huda Juned, a central NCP leader, told Prothom Alo that their vehicles were parked on the road behind the hall and in the car park. After the event, they were making their way towards their vehicles when Awami League leaders and activists, who had already gathered there, launched a sudden attack on them.

On the other hand, Sushanta Das Gupta, an Awami League-affiliated online activist, told Prothom Alo that they were standing on the road behind the hall when an argument broke out between them and a security guard. He claimed that the incident began when the security guard pushed an Awami League activist during the altercation.

Sushanta Das Gupta also claimed that, since 5 August, his home in Habiganj, Bangladesh, had been set on fire twice. He said this was why he had come to protest at Nahid's event.

Local resident Karin also said she had seen a security guard speaking rudely to people gathered there. However, she did not say whether the guard had pushed anyone.

Following the incident, several posts by Awami League leaders, activists and supporters on social media contained expressions of jubilation.

Anwaruzzaman Chowdhury, joint general secretary of the UK Awami League and former mayor of Sylhet City Corporation, wrote in a Facebook post after the incident, “A united Awami League is strong, well-organised and unstoppable. Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu.”

However, some senior leaders of the UK Awami League have expressed embarrassment over the clashes surrounding Nahid Islam's civic reception.

At least two senior UK Awami League leaders, speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, said that such an incident was entirely undesirable.

According to the two leaders, the protest against Nahid Islam's visit to the United Kingdom had not been organised under the party's banner. Supporters of the party had arranged the programme. They had also discouraged supporters from organising such protests.

Questions rose over police absence after the event

Police officers were present at the front and rear of the Mayfair venue before the event began because of concerns about possible clashes. However, eyewitness accounts suggest that the police presence had diminished by the time the two groups began fighting after the event.

Several people aware of the incident have questioned why the police did not maintain their presence after the event, despite the tension that had already been building. They believe that the violence might have been avoided had the police maintained the same level of deployment after the event as they had before it began.

Quoting a statement from the London Police, British media reported that police received a report of disorder on High Road in Romford at 9:59 pm on Monday. According to the police, around 50 men had taken part in a protest before the violence began.

Police said they took three people to hospital following the incident. None of their injuries was life-threatening or likely to have a life-changing impact.

The London Ambulance Service said it received an emergency call at 10:12 pm and dispatched two ambulance crews to the scene. Paramedics treated six people at the location, one of whom they took to a local hospital.

Al Huda Welfare Foundation UK stands at the eastern junction of Cedar Park Gardens, beside the Mayfair venue. The Islamic religious institution has a mosque and a madrasah.

Hossain, a Bangladeshi worshipper at the mosque, told Prothom Alo that several local residents had condemned the behaviour of Bangladeshis to him following the incident. He said their comments had left him feeling ashamed as a Bangladeshi.

Hossain has lived in the area for many years and enjoys good relations with local residents. He said he hoped Bangladeshis would never again become involved in such incidents on British soil.

Over 100 IEDs, weapons, ammunition seized in Teknaf, 2 detained
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has seized more than 100 improvised explosive devices (IEDs), materials used to make explosives, firearms and a large quantity of ammunition during an operation in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar.
Two auto-rickshaw drivers were detained, while a motorcycle and two auto-rickshaws allegedly used by the suspects were seized.
Colonel Anwar Ul Alam, sector commander of BGB’s Ramu Sector, confirmed the operation and the seizures on Sunday morning.
According to BGB sources, personnel from the 2nd BGB Battalion under the Ramu Sector conducted the operation based on a tip-off.
The recovered items include a foreign-made pistol, a locally made firearm and 254 rounds of ammunition. The force also seized materials used to manufacture IEDs, including steel casings, electrical wires and specialised toolkits.
The BGB suspects that an organised group had stockpiled the weapons and explosives to carry out acts of sabotage amid the current situation in the country.
According to BGB sources, the group had procured the items from neighbouring Myanmar.
The force believes the IEDs and explosive-making materials were stockpiled for potential sabotage. However, details about the interrogation of the two detainees and their alleged involvement have not yet been disclosed.
Colonel Anwar Ul Alam said legal proceedings were underway over the seizure and the detention of the two individuals.

item.title: Govt revises education allowances for officials’ children abroad
item.description:
The government has revised monthly education allowances for children of government officials and employees working at the country’s diplomatic missions abroad, increasing the financial support according to the location of the mission and the children’s level of education.
The Finance Division issued an order on November 19, setting out revised allowance rates for officials serving in 84 Bangladesh missions abroad.
Under the revised structure, missions have been divided into four categories, with monthly allowances varying according to the cost and location of education.
For missions under category "A", covering 15 missions, the monthly allowance for one child studying up to A-level has been fixed at $250, while the rate for two children is $350. At the university level, the allowance is $250 for one child and $380 for two children.
For category "B", covering 41 missions, the monthly allowance is $210 for one child and $310 for two children at the school level. The corresponding rates for university students are $210 and $320.
For category "C", covering 19 missions, the allowance has been set at $210 for one child and $280 for two children at both school and university levels.
For the remaining nine missions under category "D", the monthly allowance is $200 for one child and $250 for two children at the school level. At the university level, the rates are $210 for one child and $250 for two children.
The order stipulates that the existing arrangement requiring officials and employees to bear 15% of their children’s actual education expenses will remain in force.
It also says where English is not the medium of instruction in a country, but an official arranges English-medium education for their children in another English-speaking country, the prescribed allowance for the relevant mission will apply.
The allowance will be payable for a maximum of two children at a time. No allowance will be provided if a child receives education remotely or through digital platforms instead of attending an educational institution.
The Finance Division said other existing conditions governing education allowances would remain unchanged and the revised order would take effect immediately.

item.title: Workers return to work in Savar-Ashulia, 23 factories remain closed
item.description:
Garment workers returned to their workplaces in Savar and Ashulia on Sunday amid ongoing labour unrest over demands for a minimum wage, with the industrial areas witnessing a largely peaceful start to the second working day of the week.
Workers were seen entering factories as usual in the morning, with no major disturbances reported across the industrial belt.
However, 23 garment factories remained closed following isolated incidents, despite an improvement in the situation compared to the previous day.
Of the factories, 21 were shut under the “no work, no pay” provision in Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006. The remaining two declared general holidays after workers did not report for duty.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Industrial Police-1, confirmed the information.
Industrial Police officials expressed hope that the peaceful situation would continue, although stability would largely depend on workers' participation in production activities.
Meanwhile, law enforcement personnel remained on high alert at key points across the industrial belt and outside factories to prevent any untoward incidents.

item.title: Tribunal to issue order on Masud Uddin’s CMH treatment plea on November 25
item.description:
The hearing on a petition filed by retired lieutenant general Masud Uddin Chowdhury, an accused in a crimes against humanity case, seeking transfer from Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) to the Combined Military Hospital (CMH) for treatment has concluded.
International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Sunday set November 25 for passing an order on the petition.
During the hearing, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam told the tribunal that the defence had sought permission for Masud Uddin to receive treatment at CMH.
However, he argued that CMH lacked the necessary security arrangements for patients in the custody of prison authorities. In contrast, Bangladesh Medical University (BMU)—formerly known as Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) and DMCH have facilities for police surveillance to ensure the security of detainees receiving treatment.
He suggested that treatment at either of the two hospitals would therefore be more appropriate.
On November 11, defence counsel Liton Ahmed argued that Masud Uddin had been suffering from blood cancer for a long time and also had kidney complications requiring regular dialysis, as advised by his doctors.
He had also developed heart-related complications and required specialised and continuous medical care, the lawyer said.
Major (retd) Mozaffar Hossain has also been arrested and is being held in connection with the case. The tribunal has directed that investigation reports concerning both accused be submitted by November 23.
According to the prosecution, Mozaffar maintained regular contact with Masud Uddin during the July mass uprising, when a massacre took place in Feni. Investigators have found evidence of their involvement in the incident, the prosecution said.
Earlier, on July 21, the prosecution sought a production warrant to formally show Mozaffar Hossain arrested in the case. He is also an accused in the case over the assassination of former president Ziaur Rahman.
On the night of March 23 this year, the Detective Branch (DB) of police arrested Masud Uddin Chowdhury from his residence in Baridhara DOHS in Dhaka.
He is known as one of the key figures behind the political transition of January 11, 2007, commonly referred to as 1/11.

item.title: PM: Development impossible without SME production, marketing
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said national development is impossible without production and marketing in the small and medium enterprise (SME) sector, which has played a key role in the progress of many European countries.
Against this backdrop, the government is taking various initiatives to promote SME growth. The draft National SME Policy 2026 is expected to receive Cabinet approval soon, with the aim of transforming Bangladesh into a manufacturing hub and export gateway.
Tarique Rahman made the remarks while inaugurating the National SME Product Fair at the China-Bangladesh Friendship Exhibition Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Sunday.
Organised by the Ministry of Industries under the theme “Prosperity through SMEs, Growth for the Economy”, the fair features 380 entrepreneurs.
The prime minister said the SME sector was a key priority for the government and that there was no alternative to its development in building an economically prosperous country.
However, he identified a lack of capital and technology, difficulties in accessing loans and a shortage of skilled workers as major barriers to SME development, production and marketing.
He said providing loans on favourable terms, offering incentives and promoting public-private partnerships could help address these challenges.
The government aims to increase the SME sector's contribution to the national economy to 35%, a move expected to create 2.5 million jobs, he added.
Industries Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir chaired the event, while Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and FBCCI Administrator Md Fazlul Haque attended as special guests.
Abdun Naser Khan, secretary of the Ministry of Industries and chairperson of the SME Foundation, said developing the SME sector was essential to making Bangladesh's economic growth more inclusive, dynamic and sustainable.

item.title: 95 platoons of BGB deployed in seven districts, including Gopalganj
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has deployed 95 platoons across seven districts, including two battalions in Gopalganj, to maintain law and order, ensure public security, and handle any untoward situation.
The deployment, made following instructions from the Ministry of Home Affairs, also covers Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Mymensingh, Faridpur and Cox’s Bazar districts, according to a BGB press release issued on Sunday.
The deployed BGB personnel are performing their duties in coordination with the respective district administration and other law enforcement agencies.
Security and surveillance have been strengthened at key installations, industrial areas and other important locations in the districts to prevent disorder, violence and activities that could pose a threat to public security, the release said.
Meanwhile, the BGB headquarters is maintaining technology-based surveillance through its monitoring cell to closely monitor the situation on the ground and ensure coordination.
Live footage collected through drones, body-worn cameras and other modern technologies is being monitored round the clock, according to the release.
It said BGB members were performing their assigned duties in maintaining internal law and order alongside their regular responsibilities at the borders, with the highest level of professionalism, discipline and patience.
The force remained committed to ensuring the safety of people's lives and property, keeping normal movement and daily activities uninterrupted, and taking necessary precautionary measures to deal with any untoward situation, the release added.

item.title: Messi furore after Columbus thrash Miami in MLS Cup
item.description:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.
Messi's frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.
Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.
"Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card," Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. "It's just really sad."
Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow.
"The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct," Chapman told a pool reporter.
Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia's early penalty.
Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami's Nu Stadium.
The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.
"It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards.
"We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added.
"There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character."
In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.
The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday.
US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia.
Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring.
New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday.

item.title: Pant ton drives India to record 720-9dec against New Zealand
item.description:
India scored the highest innings total in Test matches in New Zealand on Sunday, declaring at a mammoth 720-9 on Sunday midway through the fourth afternoon of the first Test in Wellington, after Rishabh Pant's blistering 128.
New Zealand were 33-1 in their second innings at tea, with captain Tom Latham falling in the first over, needing another 319 runs to avoid an innings defeat with four sessions to go.
Henry Nicholls was 21 not out and Devon Conway on 12 at the break after Latham registered a dreaded "pair" of ducks, out for nought second ball for the second time in the game when he edged Jasprit Bumrah to Pant.
India surpassed the previous record for Tests in New Zealand, the hosts' 715-6 declared against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019.
It was the 18th highest innings in Test history.
Dhruv Jurel was the last man out, stumped from the bowling of Glenn Phillips for a brisk 78 off 79 balls.
Pant was the star of the morning, falling off the last ball before lunch as India reached the break on 629-6.
The diminutive wicketkeeper brought up his hundred by lofting Glenn Phillips over long-off for six, before kissing the badge of his helmet and pointing to the sky.
It was his ninth hundred in Test cricket, and included 10 fours and six sixes.
Pant had been 55 not out overnight alongside Anshul Kamboj, who was yet to score but took on the role of aggressor with a flurry of lofted drives and outright slogs.
He fell for a swift 38 from 42 balls, hitting six fours and a six, bringing Dhruv Jurel to the crease and prompting Pant to come out of his shell.
He whacked Phillips out of the Basin Reserve ground, the ball seen running down neighbouring Cambridge Terrace alongside the Sunday morning traffic.
Jurel was 32 not out when Pant was dismissed on the brink of lunch, caught by Nathan Smith at deep midwicket from Rachin Ravindra's bowling after facing 153 balls.
Ravindra ended with 2-44 from 10 overs, while Glenn Phillips took 3-154 in 24 overs.
Seamer Jacob Duffy conceded the second most runs in an innings by a bowler in New Zealand Test history, returning 1-201 from 33 overs.
Each of India's top five batsmen had scores of 80 or higher, the first time that has happened in a Test.
KL Rahul made 136 opening the batting alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal, who made 85.
Devdutt Padikkal scored 80 and Shubman Gill 98, before Pant's hundred on day four.

item.title: Nmecha helps Dortmund beat Gladbach to top Bundesliga
item.description:
Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.
Bayern Munich's 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha's late strike.
Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points.
Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday's draw, with the Ballon d'Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday.
Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck urged his teammates not to get too far ahead of themselves, despite overtaking Bayern.
"The season is only truly decided from March or April onwards. We need to be in the mix by then," he told reporters.
Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach.
Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz.
With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post.
Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz's fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points.
Igor Matanovic's 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern.
Last season's Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin.
Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday.
Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp's Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital.
Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen's 4-0 home win over Paderborn.
Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen's first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez.
Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals.
In Saturday's late game, Schalke played out a scoreless home draw with Stuttgart.
Promoted in the summer, Schalke are yet to score a goal in five home matches.
Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home.
Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive.
Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga's 64-year history.

item.title: Nadal appointment confirmed at Real Madrid general assembly
item.description:
Retired tennis superstar Rafael Nadal joined Real Madrid's board of directors on Saturday after his appointment was ratified at the club's general assembly.
Nadal, a 22-time Grand Slam winner, has been an honorary club member since 2011 and shares a strong relationship with Madrid president Florentino Perez.
"I want to thank the president. When you named me honorary member it was very special, and today is one step further," said Nadal.
"For me, it's a great responsibility. Real Madrid is passed down from parents to children -- it's something that brings people together. And now, having this chance is an enormous opportunity."
President Perez said Nadal's appointment would help keep the club succeeding long into the future.
"His arrival is more than just the signing of an extraordinary figure -- it means that one of the greatest legends wants to share our future with us," said Perez.
"I am convinced that his presence will help us continue building the Real Madrid we want for the generations to come."
Nadal, 40, won a record 14 French Open singles titles in a glittering career.
In 2023 Nadal said one day he would like to be Madrid president, but did not know if he was qualified for the post.
Ahead of club elections this year Nadal distanced himself from reports that he would stand as a candidate. Perez triumphed in June, beating Enrique Riquelme.

item.title: Espi snatches late Real Madrid win over Celta Vigo
item.description:
Carlos Espi pounced to claim Real Madrid a late 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo in La Liga on Saturday, pulling Los Blancos level on points with leaders Barcelona.
The Spanish champions face Villarreal on Sunday looking to restore their three-point advantage over Jose Mourinho's in-form Madrid, who have won nine consecutive games across all competitions.
Espi, who has often provided vital contributions from the bench this season, helped Madrid complete a comeback at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium after Pablo Duran put the visitors ahead early on.
French superstar Kylian Mbappe missed a first-half penalty on a frustrating night for Madrid's top goalscorer.
However, Jude Bellingham pulled Madrid level before Espi netted in the 85th minute to claim the three points for his team.
"It's a dream day, I really wanted to (score) here at home in front of all the Madrid fans, it's a day I dreamed of, I'm really happy," Espi told Real Madrid TV.
"I try to do what the coach asks me, I'll give the most I can and take advantage of every minute that I'm given, and if I can help the team, then it's even better."
Mourinho began with Vinicius Junior on the bench, with the Brazilian eligible in La Liga again after a four-match ban for hair pulling, and the winger made contributions to both of Madrid's goals in a bright substitute appearance.
Celta Vigo took a surprise lead, through Spanish forward Duran in the sixth minute.
The Galicians carved open Madrid's defence with a slick attack, finished by Duran after Williot Swedberg played the ball through Dean Huijsen's legs and across the face of goal.
Madrid had a good chance to equalise when Yan Diomande whipped in a dangerous cross which Bernardo Silva sent wide with a diving header.
An even better one went begging when Mbappe won and then spurned a penalty.
The French forward was tugged back in the box by Javi Rodriguez but fired the resulting spot-kick high over the crossbar, his second penalty miss of the season.
Former tennis star Rafael Nadal, appointed to the club's board earlier in the day at Madrid's general assembly, pressed his hand to his forehead in disbelief.
- Super sub Espi -
Mourinho sent on Vinicius early in the second half as part of a triple change, with record signing Diomande switching to the right flank.
Vinicius was involved in Madrid's equaliser 10 minutes later, feeding Mbappe, who teed up Bellingham to power into the bottom corner for his fifth league goal.
Eduardo Camavinga sent a shot scuttling narrowly wide of the near post as Madrid tried to force their way in front, with Celta sitting ever deeper.
Eventually it came when Bellingham drove forward and laid the ball off to Vinicius, who swung in a cross to target man Espi, signed in the summer from Levante.
Although Celta goalkeeper Ionut Radu saved Espi's header, the forward stayed alert to tuck home the rebound.
It was Espi's third league goal of the season, each of which have led to Madrid claiming late victories.
"Madrid are a team with a lot of quality, they put you under the cosh... but we let go something that we thought we could take away (from here)," Celta's Duran told Movistar.
Earlier, Kike Salas struck late to save a point for Sevilla in a 1-1 derby draw against Real Betis.
Manuel Pellegrini's Betis, fourth, had taken the lead through Antony's deflected effort early in the second half.
However, hosts Sevilla, sixth, equalised in the 91st minute with Salas's low drive, which Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles somehow let squeeze past him.
"We let two points slip away in the final minutes with a completely avoidable goal," grumbled Pellegrini.
Valencia earned a 1-0 win at Rayo Vallecano to provisionally move out of the relegation zone. Alaves defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-1 to climb up to eighth.

item.title: City stumble again in Fulham draw, Arsenal held by Newcastle
item.description:
Manchester City's winless Premier League run extended to four games after a damaging 1-1 draw against Fulham, while leaders Arsenal were held to a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.
Third-placed City trail six points behind Arsenal as their title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules.
The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal.
After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca's reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City's quest to topple Arsenal.
Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz at the Etihad Stadium.
City were furious that Erling Haaland's equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno.
Elliot Anderson's sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display.
"Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it's for sure something we need to improve," said Maresca.
At St James' Park, Eberechi Eze put Arsenal ahead in the 33rd minute with a clinical close-range finish from Kai Havertz's pass.
But Newcastle rocked Mikel Arteta's men in the second half.
Harvey Barnes fired Newcastle's 49th-minute equaliser from William Osula's pass after Arsenal midfielder Martin Odegaard conceded possession cheaply.
When Dan Burn headed down from Lewis Hall's corner, Malick Thiaw pounced to give Newcastle the lead with a 62nd-minute tap-in.
Noni Madueke saved Arsenal from only their second league defeat this season, cutting inside for a low drive that eluded Lukas Hornicek's weak attempted save in the 78th minute.
Arsenal are six points above second-placed Brighton, who can close the gap with a win at Hull on Sunday.
"We needed to raise our level in the second half when the opponent had a reaction but we were below the level," said Arteta, who lost 'keeper David Raya to a second half shoulder injury.
"Individually we had some good performances but it was not enough."
- Chelsea on the rocks -
Leeds climbed to sixth place after coming from behind to stun Chelsea with a 4-1 win at Stamford Bridge.
Emmanuel Emegha's first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny.
Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot.
Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals.
"We need to be tougher. It's something mandatory in this competition. Today we were in a fragile moment mentally," Alonso said.
Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.
Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries' winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.
Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi's men.
Thomas Frank's arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles' fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.
Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.
Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday with the Red Devils second bottom of the table.
